$comment: v2.3 plan 03. Every place in src/runtime, src/wizard, src/extraction and src/generation (V3) that writes AFTER an await — methods, function declarations, and since V3 arrow functions (named by where they live) and property assignments, and what has been done about it. Generated set, hand-classified status. The guard in src/runtime/ownership.guard.test.ts fails when this file and the code disagree, in EITHER direction: a new site nobody classified, a row whose site is gone, a "checked" row with no token check in its body, or a "todo" row that has quietly acquired one (flip it to checked). Statuses: checked (verifies a RunToken before writing) | delegate (awaits a censused site that owns the check) | local (writes nothing that outlives the call) | todo (owed work). WHAT "checked" MEANS, PRECISELY: the body contains a token check -- NOT that every write is preceded by one. The detector is a body-level scan, so it cannot see the interleaving, and a body that gains a fifth host step can escape the checks that guard the other four (found 2026-09-22 in EffectsApplier.applyCheckpoint: the preset sat below the Author Note await and the background below applyCastChanges per-member awaits). Per-write checking is proven by TESTS in the case files (effectsOwnership.review.test.ts pins each check with a case that reaches it), which is also the file-level rule: a check without a case is a check a mutation can delete.

src/extraction/scheduler.ts#ExtractionSc.note: v2.3 replan V3 (2026-09-23): COVERED: the read's guard is minted before runSharedRead and travels into applyExtractionAudit, which refuses a lapsed read before any write (V2); the install-wide pause and the panel's lastError are both written only when the epoch the job started in is still current (sameWorld). NOT COVERED: `inFlight` is one flag per scheduler, so a new world's queue waits for an old job to finish (serial by design: one endpoint), and `job.run` bodies are censused where they are defined, not here. v2.4 plan 03 D2 (2026-09-24): the read's guard now carries a live signal into the model call, so a mutation inside its window or a new world ABORTS the host request (runOwner.abort.test.ts); a lapse is not retried, writes no lastError and never reaches the pause path (scheduler.test.ts "an aborted read is not retried and records no error"); an in-flight answer that wins the race against the abort is still refused at the write edge.

v2.3 replan V3 (2026-09-23): COVERED: lastHeavyError is written only when the job's starting epoch is still current (it used to land in the next world's panel after clearForNewWorld emptied it). NOT COVERED: heavyInFlight serialises across worlds by design, and the job's own writes live in its run closure, censused at its definition. v2.4 plan 03 D2 (2026-09-24): a lapsed heavy job (aborted by the epoch) is not retried and writes no lastHeavyError.

v2.3 plan 11 §Fault matrix: found by the census, not by a journey. The model call runs for minutes and every write below it resolved to whichever chat was open when it answered, so a chain generated for chat A was filed into chat B's cache and merged into chat B's story — the last async coordinator without a token. Checked after the generation and again in the catch and before the persist, because the failure path is a write too. The `generating` marker written before the await still stays in chat A after a switch, but since v2.4 plan 03 D4 it no longer blocks its key: the in-memory live-job map (a RunGuard per key, released in `finally`) is what queue() consults, and a marker no live job of this world holds is re-queued on return; hydrate demotes a persisted queued/generating entry (sanitizeExpansion). The `finally` release is in-memory only (local).

src/runtime/coordinators/extractionCoord.note: v2.3 plan 03: the main extraction write path. verifyEntries is a judge pass, and everything after it deposits the read conclusions into the memory tiers, the epistemic and ledger stores and the audit ring. Minted with the audit window: these entries are claims ABOUT the messages read, so an edit inside that span invalidates them while a reply appended after it does not. Re-checked after every awaited stage (verify, applyEntries, save) rather than once, because a single check on the near side of an await is what C1 was. RESIDUAL: enqueueExtractorDeltas runs before the await and is not covered.

v2.3 plan 03: TWO model calls with a store written in between, so the check sits after each call rather than once at the end — the epistemic signals are applied before the ledger prompt is even sent. Both stores and the injection update are refused when the world moved.

v2.3 replan V3 (2026-09-23): mints one read over the whole chat before the first await, asks it before every window, passes it into applyAudit (which refuses a lapsed read before any write), and asks again before the final read, the boundary commit and the error record. It used to read the NEXT chat's windows into memory after a switch. v2.4 plan 03 D4 (2026-09-24): the loop moved to memorizeWindows and the exit to endBacklog, so every ending passes through one write. The read it hands on is the chat token AND the backlog's own Stop controller (cancelMemorizeBacklog), checked between windows. Its only write after the await is clearing its own in-memory `backlogStop` handle. v2.4 plan 03 D5 wiring (2026-09-24): the read is minted BEFORE the plan's token count (an await), and the preflight popup is another await before anything is sent; the plan is refused when the read lapsed during either. The model calls now carry anySignal([Stop, read.signal]), so Stop and a mutation inside the whole-chat window cancel the request in flight (budgetWiring.review.test.ts).

v2.4 plan 03 D4 (2026-09-24): the backlog's one exit. Reads read.lapsed() BEFORE its only write: an epoch/chat/story lapse writes nothing (the backfill it would clear belongs to another chat, whose hydrate resets running itself); a same-chat lapse (window: an edit or swipe inside the whole-chat read; version: a hot-swapped story) and a player Stop write running:false with a reason. This is what closes the same-chat wedge, where every early return left running:true until reload.

v2.4 plan 03 D4 (2026-09-24): the V3 window loop, moved out of runMemorizeBacklog unchanged. The ReadOwnership it is handed combines the whole-chat token with the Stop controller, and it is asked before every window, after every applyAudit (which refuses a lapsed read before any write), before the final read and before the boundary commit. A stopped run therefore writes nothing further, and the windows already applied stay (memory-only, acceptedDeltas: []).

v2.3 replan V2 (2026-09-23): the read is minted BEFORE runSharedRead over the exact window it reads; applyAudit refuses a lapsed read before any write, and the boundary commit is skipped when the read lapsed.

v2.3 plan 03: beginRun with the audit window; a summary describing an edited or departed window is discarded before it reaches the memory tiers. v2.4 plan 03 D5 wiring (2026-09-24): the guard's window widens to the whole scene [previous scene end + 1, break], and the map -> reduce loop (memory/sceneSummary.ts) asks stillOwns() INSIDE the loop before every model call; the coordinator asks again before the write (budgetWiring.review.test.ts "an edit before the detecting window but inside the scene discards the summary").

src/runtime/effectHost.ts#restoreEffectT.note: PARTIAL: one inverse per effect target, and the GUARD IS THE CALLER. `EffectsApplier.restoreEffects` reads each target's current value and compares it with what this chat wrote before calling anything here, and refuses the ones that no longer hold it — so a restore that outlived its chat cannot overwrite an edit someone else made. The token would add the chat-switch case, which the leave/rollback/restart callers own; each branch here is a single stHost seam whose own result is returned as the answer.

src/runtime/effectsApplier.ts#EffectsApp.note: PARTIAL: guarded entirely from its CALLER. Its own body has no await before the write, so a guard inside would mint at the moment of the write and prove nothing; commitBoundary checks ownsOpenChat before calling it. Any new caller must do the same.

NOT COVERED: none beyond withLedger's own row.

v2.3 plan 03: the widest write edge in the extension -- World Info flags in shared lorebook FILES, Authors Note and preset as install state, and cast_changes mutating the GROUP disabled_members, which outlives the chat. Checked before EVERY host-facing write rather than once per group of them (2026-09-22: the preset sat below the Author Note await and the background below applyCastChanges per-member awaits with no check between, so the background was the one write that could land in another chat; it now checks per member inside the loop, before the preset, and before the background). It stops rather than completing, because whatever moved the world runs its own applyCheckpoint.

v2.3 plan 03: the only effect that SPEAKS — fireReply posts a message into whatever chat is open, so a late fire is visible in the transcript. One await per reply, so the check is inside the loop. Limit: beginRun mints at entry, so it detects the world moving DURING the sequence, not before; the caller owns that decision. Live-proven 2026-09-20: plan02-runtime scenario green twice against a group with the required cast, npcFired=1 — the guard does not suppress a real scripted reply. The trigger (generating) branch is still unproven live.
v2.3 replan V3 (2026-09-23): awaits applyWorldInfo, handing it the caller's run; applyWorldInfo checks before each write.

PARTIAL: the COMPARE-AND-SET is the guard, and it is stronger than a token. Before anything is written back, the host's current value is read and compared with what this chat wrote; a target that no longer holds it is refused and marked externally-changed rather than overwritten. What the token would add is the chat-switch case, and the caller owns that decision: `restoreEffects` runs from the leave/restart/rollback path, which re-reads the world it is leaving, and every host write it performs is delegated to the injected `restore` (a stHost seam).

v2.3 replan V3 (2026-09-23): restore runs BECAUSE the world moved (leave/exit/restart/rollback), so a token would refuse exactly the work it exists for. COVERED: host writes go through restoreEffects' compare-and-set; the mirror write targets the captured departing `extras`; appliedChat is reset only when this chat's effects are gone. NOT COVERED: two restores racing each other are ordered by the ledger status, not by a token.

v2.3 plan 06: the write-ahead wrapper every recorded host effect goes through. It awaits ChatSave.persist (through the manager's persist delegate), which owns the check; its other writes are the ledger row it appends and the status it sets, both THIS chat's own in-memory state, patched before the first await — so a token minted here would be compared against the world it was just minted from, which is the reason `MemoryCoordinator.commit` gives.

src/runtime/effectsApplier.ts#applyWorld.note: v2.3 replan V3 (2026-09-23): the plan spans several books and each is two host writes; the caller's run is now asked before EVERY write (it used to be checked once, after the whole loop). Callers: applyCheckpoint and releaseWorldInfo pass their run.

src/runtime/loreSelect.ts#LoreSelector.f.note: v2.3 plan 11 §Fault matrix: split out of select() so a refused force is reported instead of discarded, and so the token check sits where the write is. Both callers (the fresh path and the cached re-force) minted the run and pass it in, so the cached path — which had NO token check at all before this — is covered too. The story swap that the cached path could not see is fixed in the CACHE KEY, not here: a token minted at the start of a call can never notice that a cache entry was built under a story the chat has since left.

src/runtime/loreSelect.ts#LoreSelector.s.note: v2.3 plan 03 (C1, the lore surface). force() pushes entries into the NEXT generation, so a selection outliving its chat seeds another chat prompt with this story lore. Invisible to the census until 2026-09-20 because its write verb is force, which WRITE_NAME did not list — the plan text named it and the regex did not. v2.3 plan 11 moved the check one hop: select() mints the run and awaits LoreSelector.forced, which owns the check and sits where the write is.

src/runtime/memoryMirror.ts#syncMemoryMi.note: v2.3 plan 03: it already had a hand-rolled chat comparison guarding the binding, which the census could not see and which only asked about the chat. A story swap inside the same chat passed it, and the mirror book is per-chat but shared across stories. The comparison is kept (it is the only guard an unwired host has) and the token check added beside it.

src/runtime/mirrorReaper.ts#MirrorReaper.note: v2.4 plan 02 T14 (2026-09-24): deletes a deleted chat's per-chat mirror book. Its world is not the open chat (that chat is gone, and ST opens another before it announces a solo delete), so the run is minted from `lifetimeOwnership()`, which only `stopRuntime` lapses. `run.stillOwns()` is checked after the player's confirm and immediately before `deleteLorebook`, so a reap whose runtime stopped while the popup was open deletes nothing and leaves a Repair row (mirrorReaper.review.test.ts "deletes nothing once the runtime stopped while the confirm was open"). The evidence guards sit before the confirm: the `so-owner` marker must name the deleted chat, and `probeChat` must read the chat file as absent (02-H11: an announce without a delete is refused). `notify` only re-renders; the orphan registry is session memory, not any chat's.

src/runtime/memoryQueue.ts#commitDecisio.note: v2.4 plan 02 (seed D), was partial since v2.3 plan 05. Owns the write for every author decision (resolve, dismiss, Store anyway, reconfirm, discard). The put-back runs only on evidence of a lost write, and is now checked twice: a run token minted at the top with NO window (the row is named by the author, so the token asks only whether the chat, story, version or epoch moved -- an edited message cannot lapse it), re-checked before the put-back, so a decision whose chat was left during the save puts nothing into the next chat's memory; and a per-row compare-and-set, `{store, before: Map<id,row|ABSENT>, wrote: Map<id,row|ABSENT>}` built by diffStore, so a row goes back only while it still IS the row this decision wrote, a row another writer added during the save is kept, and one it changed is left alone and reported externally-changed (memoryQueue.test.ts, seed D block). The host-facing write awaits MemoryCoordinator.save, which awaits ChatSave.persist, where the chat check for the write itself lives.

src/runtime/requirementsWatch.ts#refresh.note: v2.4 plan 02 §8 (2026-09-24). The between-turns requirements refresh the watch runs 250 ms after PERSONA_CHANGED / GROUP_UPDATED / WORLDINFO_SETTINGS_UPDATED. Its RunGuard is minted when the host event arrives (RequirementsWatch.schedule), so a chat left inside the debounce refreshes nothing; checked again after the hydrate apply (before persist) and after the persist (before notify). The hydrate apply itself is EffectsApplier.applyCheckpoint, which checks its own token before each host step. Ready -> not-ready writes nothing but the in-memory requirements and a notify. Cases: requirementsWatch.test.ts "a chat left while the checkpoint was applied is not saved into", "a chat left inside the debounce refreshes nothing for it".

src/runtime/rollback.ts#runRollback.note: v2.4 plan 02 §10 (2026-09-24): the wrapper around `rollbackOnce` (which carries the old runRollback row). Its only write after the await is `deps.notices.lastOutcome`, an in-memory record of the outcome the harness reads for `expect.rollbackOutcome`; it is never persisted and names no chat, so there is no edge for a token to guard.

src/runtime/rollback.ts#rollbackOnce.note: v2.3 plan 04. The rollback composition, extracted from the manager for its line budget. Partial, not checked: it verifies no token of its own, because it does not start any work — it is the mutation's own consequence. `rollbackFromMessage` records the mutation position on the owner before calling it, the run it composes belongs to the chat the runtime is loaded for, and every host write it triggers (world-info re-apply, stagecraft revert) is one this census already covers at its own edge. Making it `checked` means minting a token inside work that the mutation just invalidated, which would refuse the rollback it exists to perform.

src/runtime/rollback.ts#rollbackOnce.una.note: v2.3 replan V11 (2026-09-23). The E1 path, shared by both ways the history can be gone (nothing retained precedes the edit, or the boundary it names has no snapshot). Partial for the same reason as `runRollback`: it is the mutation's own consequence, so minting a token inside it would refuse the rollback it exists to perform. Its one host write that can cross a chat, the stagecraft revert, is `revertAppliedSince`, which checks the token before each inverse; `persist` carries the chat check.
